correctness.rationale: The multiplication e_i^2=e_(i+1) (i<n) and e_i e_j=0 for i!=j makes the weight-zero identity force diagonal-plus-terminal operator matrices. Nonzero diagonal entries form a terminal geometric string d_(i+1)=d_i/2, with terminal coefficients zero after the first nonzero diagonal except at its pivot. The annihilator-valued class contributes q^n maps, and pivot families contribute sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(q−1)q^k=q^n−q, giving 2q^n−q. All automorphisms have phi(e1)=a e1+t en and phi(e_i)=a^{2^{i−1}}e_i (i>=2). Their conjugation fixes the diagonal and acts affinely on terminal coefficients: b1 → a^{L−1}b1 +(d1−dn)t/a and b_i→a^{L−2^{i−1}}b_i. Burnside over F_q^×⋉F_q splits strata, with multiplicative weights w_i=L−2^{i−1}; the exceptional pivot resonance occurs exactly when char(F_q) divides L−1. The resulting totient-weighted divisor sums define B_k and C_n and yield O_n(q)=(q−1)[T_n+sum_{k=2}^{n−1}B_k+B_{n−1}]+C_n. Exact checks independently verified operator equations and group orbits for (n,q)=(3,3),(3,5),(4,3),(4,5),(5,3), with respective orbit counts 22,36,62,176,190; and a nonprime GF(9) orbit check for n=3 found 76 orbits among 1,449 operators. These computations corroborate, rather than prove, all n,q.

originality.rationale: Qaralleh, Mukhamedov and Khakimov (Jan 2026), Theorem 4.5 and subsequent June 2026 follow-up Theorems 2.4/6.4, are close *same-family* precedents. They already classify ordinary Rota–Baxter operators and determine automorphism-fixed (commuting) coefficients over characteristic-zero fields, which supplies much of the conceptual input and might simplify a Burnside derivation. The new theorem does not claim the raw operator normal form, automorphism group or commutant equations as original. It extends to every odd finite field, extracts all conjugacy orbits with characteristic-dependent resonance and a closed q=3 formula. The June commutant theorem is over characteristic zero and does not itself state or quantify finite-field orbits; direct implication of the finite-field count would require a field extension argument plus nontrivial weighted fixed-point counting. Novelty is therefore accepted narrowly and qualified; do not conflate centralizer equations with a completed orbit census.
